summary: Round r1 (restricted network). All empirical items pending. The single WebSearch located the only Nepal-specific resilience BCR study found so far: Rai et al. (2020), a household-survey cost-benefit analysis of the Lower Karnali flood early-warning system (IJDRR; full text on DPNet); its values are not recorded because they appeared only in search snippets. EWS coverage leads: DHM flood forecasting portal, BIPAD real-time layers, ICIMOD/UNDP PDGL inventory, UNDP CFGORRP GLOF project, World Bank/CIF hydromet project results. Adaptation finance reuses 25D channels (GCF, GEF/LDCF, Adaptation Fund, CIF PPCR, OECD CRS adaptation marker, MoF climate budget code) plus NDC/NAP needs; 25D owns the flow series and 13C reports only the adaptation subset and access-vs-need gap. The reported August 2026 Rasuwagadhi-Kerung flood (unverified) is noted only as a test case for transboundary GLOF warning once verified.

findings.claim: Q1a: Flood early-warning coverage — number of real-time hydrometric/rainfall stations, rivers/basins with operational forecasts, and population/households receiving SMS or siren alerts.
findings.period: as of latest DHM/NDRRMA reporting date (calendar); project results by World Bank FY
findings.note: Required: DHM station list and forecast-point list; BIPAD/NDRRMA alert statistics; World Bank/CIF hydromet project results frameworks. Coverage definitions (stations vs forecast points vs population reached) kept separate.

findings.claim: Q1b: GLOF early-warning coverage — which potentially dangerous glacial lakes have monitoring/EWS or mitigation works.
findings.note: Required: ICIMOD/UNDP 2020 PDGL list cross-tabulated with DHM/UNDP GLOF EWS installations; transboundary (TAR) lakes monitored or not, linked to 25B BA-06 data-sharing gap.

findings.claim: Q2: Benefit-cost ratios of documented resilience investments in Nepal (community flood EWS, hydromet, GLOF lake lowering, resilient roads, retrofitting).
findings.period: study year and price base as stated in each study
findings.note: Required: Rai et al. 2020 Karnali EWS CBA (BCR range, discount rate, horizon, scenario definitions) retrieved from journal or DPNet full text; CCDR resilience cost-benefit tables; global benchmarks (GCA 2019; Lifelines 2019) labelled non-Nepal. No values recorded from search snippets.

findings.claim: Q3: Adaptation finance received (disbursed) versus approved/pledged, by channel, and versus NDC/NAP needs.
findings.period: fund approval years (calendar), World Bank FY, Nepal FY for on-budget; stated per channel
findings.note: Supplied by 25D climate_finance_access (owner); 13C takes the adaptation subset only and adds needs comparison. Required: fund portals approved vs disbursed; OECD CRS adaptation-marked; NAP/NDC needs.

findings.claim: BCRs are study-specific (discount rate, horizon, counted benefit categories, counterfactual) and are not transferable across interventions or averaged; global benchmarks are labelled non-Nepal and used only to bound plausibility.
13C does not re-estimate climate finance flows; 25D owns the channel-level series and double-counting reconciliation, and 13C reports the adaptation share and access-vs-need comparison only.

Avoided losses in BCR studies are not added to 13A historical losses or 25E damage functions; they are used only to parameterise adaptation-effect multipliers (share of loss avoided) once sources are retrieved.

data_gaps: Only one Nepal-specific BCR study located (community flood EWS, Karnali); no Nepal BCR located for hydromet modernisation, GLOF lake lowering, resilient roads or retrofitting.
No consolidated national statistic on EWS population coverage identified; definition to be fixed on retrieval.
Transboundary GLOF warning coverage from TAR lakes is undocumented pending 25B BA-06 and verification of the August 2026 event.
DHM hydrology portal, UNDP CFGORRP, GCA and Lifelines URLs are from general knowledge and unverified.

assumptions.text: BCRs are carried with their study metadata and never pooled.
25D owns climate finance flows; 13C reports the adaptation subset.
Avoided losses parameterise adaptation effects only; no additive loss series.

challenges.text: Please tag each channel row with adaptation vs mitigation vs cross-cutting and approved vs disbursed so 13C can compute the adaptation access ratio without re-deriving flows.
Adaptation-effect parameters (share of hazard loss avoided by EWS) from 13C should enter 25E damage functions as multipliers under explicit adaptation assumptions, not as separate benefit lines.
GLOF early-warning for TAR-origin lakes depends on Nepal-China data sharing; please confirm whether any primary instrument exists (25B found none in r1).
Resilience investments with documented BCR above one are candidate welfare-improving actions but the single Nepal study covers only community flood EWS in one basin; do not generalise its BCR.
Request catalog entries for Practical Action, DPNet, UNDP Nepal and Global Commission on Adaptation, and verification of general-knowledge URLs.

uncertainty: High. EWS coverage lacks a standard metric; BCRs depend heavily on discount rate, horizon and which benefits are counted (household-survey avoided losses vs modelled); finance flows differ by approved/committed/disbursed basis, Rio-marker attribution and period basis (calendar vs World Bank FY vs Nepal FY).

metrics.metric: rivers/forecast points with operational flood forecast
population or households reached by alerts
PDGLs with monitoring/EWS or mitigation (incl. transboundary lakes)

ews_coverage.method: Separate station, forecast-point and population-reached metrics; basin breakdown; flag transboundary gaps.

studies.notes: to confirm whether CCDR reports BCRs

studies.intervention: EWS and other adaptation classes (global benchmark)

adaptation_finance_flows.method: Access ratio = disbursed / approved per channel (same period basis); gap vs needs reported without summing overlapping channels (MDB-channelled fund money counted once).
